## Source
.design/m5/48-tpm-signing.md — operator docs.

## Surface
- New file: `docs/operations/tpm-signing.md`
- Sections:
  1. Hardware prerequisites (Linux 6.x+, TPM 2.0 device, libtss2-esys, libtss2-tcti)
  2. PCR choice rationale (default PCR0/4/7; when to add PCR8 kernel)
  3. Init walkthrough (init CLI + publish flow)
  4. Daily ops (no operator action required; restart-zero-touch story)
  5. Firmware-update procedure (PCR change → reseal flow with offline token)
  6. Key rotation (TPM-specific notes)
  7. Multi-tenant host considerations (Q5 — TPM hierarchy allocation)
  8. Recovery procedures (lost offline token → re-init from scratch; TPM hardware failure → key migration is impossible by design, rotate to new TPM)
  9. Troubleshooting (PCR mismatch errors, tss-esapi version compatibility)

## Rust-quality notes
- Per rust-quality §8: every CLI invocation copy-pasteable; one runnable example per section.
- The docs explicitly call out: lost offline token = unrecoverable key. Operators MUST store securely (the docs include a brief storage-discipline section: paper in safe + USB stick in different location, etc.).

## External references
- v1 ops runbook (style reference): `docs/ops/runbook.md`
- TCG Linux TPM PCR documentation: https://uapi-group.org/specifications/specs/linux_tpm_pcr_registry/

## Acceptance
- [ ] `docs/operations/tpm-signing.md` exists; ≥250 lines; covers all 9 sections.
- [ ] CI markdown-lint passes.
